open_errors.issue: In ch 2 Ila tells the whole council she will give them a copy of the map, and in ch 4 she says she would have given copies 'to the queen and to the council'. This contradicts her oath to 'draw for the crown alone', her ch 9 true answer that the map goes 'to the queen, and the archive', Kunal's ch 30 line 'You swore to show the crown alone', and the ch 31 proof act, which is framed as breaking crown exclusivity for the first time. The book's proof-of-change is already announced in chapter 2.
open_errors.fix: Remove Ila's early statements that the council will get a copy.

patches.find: The crown will have a copy. I will give the council one, and every valley can read where its own roads run.
patches.replace: The crown will have it, and whoever reads it will see every road exactly where it runs.

patches.find: I'd have given a copy to the queen and to the council, and I'd have believed that was neutral.
patches.replace: I'd have given it to the queen, and I'd have believed that was neutral.

open_errors.issue: Ila has measured Kunal's pace as longer than hers by two fingers. Forty of his paces is therefore more than forty of hers, not 'thirty-odd'.

patches.find: Then I was thirty-odd out. I'll take that.
patches.replace: Then I was forty-odd out. I'll take that.

open_errors.issue: Ch 14 is about day seven of the bond, and Ila first met Kunal on the stair the eve of the Fair, two days before the binding. 'Two weeks of her careful sums' overstates the time.
open_errors.fix: Change two weeks to a week.

patches.find: Two weeks of her careful sums had taught him where she kept the small exact true things
patches.replace: A week of her careful sums had taught him where she kept the small exact true things

open_errors.issue: Ila has been in Neshar since Book 1's winter, and her commission 'came with the summer post' (ch 1). She cannot have sworn its archive oath 'in a hall in Taravan'.
open_errors.fix: Have her swear the oath at Garh Neshar, on a page sent with the commission.

patches.find: She had sworn it, on a long gold-edged page in a hall in Taravan, to take her commission
patches.replace: She had sworn it, on a long gold-edged page that came up with the summer post, before the council clerk in the Garh Neshar hall, to take her commission

open_errors.issue: Dhanu's bad leg is the left: the right foot plants and the left swings out and round (ch 7, 19, and later in ch 22). One line in ch 22 calls the right foot the stiff one.
open_errors.fix: Make the right foot the good one and the left the stiff one.

patches.find: He lowered himself onto the upturned stool with the stiff right foot first, the left swinging after.
patches.replace: He lowered himself onto the upturned stool with the good right foot first, the stiff left swinging after.

open_errors.issue: Ila and Kunal enter the Eye 'at moondown' and come out at dawn. In ch 28, Raghu's men reach the huts 'at moonrise, while you were still in the Eye', and Dhanu dies before 'the moon cleared the Kuhl shoulder'. Moonrise cannot follow moondown within a single night.
open_errors.fix: Have them enter the cleft at moonrise.

patches.find: Ila slept on the shelf in her boots, because they went into the Eye at moondown.
patches.replace: Ila slept on the shelf in her boots, because they went into the Eye at moonrise.

open_errors.issue: In the cleft (ch 23), Kunal asked Ila what she would do with the way. He did not ask her to hand him a way. Her reply 'I drew it, I don't know yet whose it is' answers the first question.

patches.find: Once, in a cleft, he had asked her to hand him a way.
patches.replace: Once, in a cleft, he had asked her what she would do with a way.

open_errors.issue: Ch 26 says Kunal's flint was left in his pack at the hut. Gauri's supplies in ch 28 include no flint, yet in ch 29 he strikes the lamp alight 'with the flint'.
open_errors.fix: Drop the flint from the list of things left at the hut, so he still has it on him.

patches.find: His pack lay at the hut, with the flint and the lamp oil and the last of the bread.
patches.replace: His pack lay at the hut, with the lamp oil and the last of the bread.

open_errors.issue: Ila tells Kunal 'The letter says the storm was an excuse.' The letter (ch 16) mentions no storm. She knows this, so the statement would be a lie to her bound partner, yet her hands stay warm throughout.

patches.find: The letter says the storm was an excuse.
patches.replace: The letter says nothing of a storm.

open_errors.issue: Kunal says 'You asked me twice about the letter.' It was Kunal who asked Ila about the letter (ch 16 and ch 21), and Kunal who paid for the second asking.

patches.find: You asked me twice about the letter and I made you pay for the asking.
patches.replace: I asked you twice about the letter and made you pay for the asking.

open_errors.issue: Raghu has eight bound pairs in all (ch 19, 24). At least three were at the lakes: Raghu with Pasang, and the two cornice pairs, one of which lost men through the ice. Eight pairs cannot still be guarding the Hollow Moon huts.
open_errors.fix: Lower the count of guards to five pairs.

patches.find: Hari's with them. Eight pairs watch the doors.
patches.replace: Hari's with them. Five pairs watch the doors.

open_errors.issue: Ila was never in Ranu with Rohan. In Book 1 she was held at Garh Neshar, and she knows him from the drafting table there.
open_errors.fix: Move her memory of Rohan to the Garh Neshar drafting table.

patches.find: She had learned in the dark of Ranu that her brother wanted a witness, not a hand.
patches.replace: She had learned at the Garh Neshar drafting table that her brother wanted a witness, not a hand.

open_errors.issue: Kiran crossed home to Shilak in ch 3, yet on day 18 he is said to be 'on the Saddle with the council's pairs', who do not cross until the thaw. At the post-council dusk scene he is said to be 'crossing with the council's pairs even now', but the council has already arrived, and ch 32 has him come up from the salt house with Roop's crew.
open_errors.fix: Kiran went back over the Saddle and returned with the council's pairs at the thaw.

patches.find: She had promised Kiran the first reading, before anyone, and Kiran was somewhere on the Saddle with the council's pairs.
patches.replace: She had promised Kiran the first reading, before anyone, and Kiran had gone back over the Saddle, to cross again with the council's pairs at the thaw.

patches.find: Kiran had asked to be told first, before anyone, where the Bargain was paid, and he was crossing with the council's pairs even now.
patches.replace: Kiran had asked to be told first, before anyone, where the Bargain was paid, and he had come over the Saddle with the council's pairs.

open_errors.issue: Sarala has reigned thirty-one winters (ch 31, F619), so she cannot have issued commissions for 'forty years'.
open_errors.fix: Change the span to her reign.

patches.find: You are the first surveyor in forty years who has made me regret a commission
patches.replace: You are the first surveyor of my reign who has made me regret a commission

open_errors.issue: Kiran addresses Ila as 'Ila-ji' (ch 1, ch 3), but ch 32 has him call her 'boss' and says he called her that all summer.

patches.find: "First on a rope's the one who falls, boss," said Kiran.
patches.replace: "First on a rope's the one who falls, Ila-ji," said Kiran.

patches.find: who sang rude songs to the links and called her *boss*.
patches.replace: who sang rude songs to the links and called her *Ila-ji*.

open_errors.issue: In ch 2 the Shepherd's Stair song's fourth line is 'Four for the fold with the broken latch', and it runs on to 'Nine and thirty', which Kunal knows. Ch 32 gives a different fourth line, says nobody sings past the fourth light, and has Kunal not know what follows five.
open_errors.fix: Frame the ch 32 lines as a separate second verse for past the fourth light.

patches.find: It's the Stair's song, but it runs on past the fourth light. Nobody sings the end.
patches.replace: It's a second verse to the Stair's song, for past the fourth light. Nobody sings it.
